subsystems.name: Thruster core
subsystems.role: the arc chamber where propellant is ionised and accelerated.

subsystems.name: Propellant feed
subsystems.role: delivers gas or vapour at a controlled rate.

subsystems.name: Power conditioning
subsystems.role: turns spacecraft bus power into very high-current, low-voltage arcs.

subsystems.name: Applied-field magnet (optional)
subsystems.role: an external coil adds magnetic field to boost thrust and efficiency.

subsystems.name: Thermal management
subsystems.role: removes waste heat from electrodes and coils.

subsystems.name: Structure and control
subsystems.role: mounts the thruster and manages operation.

buildSteps.title: Design the electrode geometry
buildSteps.detail: Cathode radius, anode shape and nozzle flare are chosen so the arc stays stable and the plasma accelerates without excessive erosion.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the electrodes
buildSteps.detail: A refractory-metal cathode (tungsten or thoriated tungsten) and a copper or refractory anode are machined and joined to cooled mounts.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the arc chamber
buildSteps.detail: Electrodes are separated by a high-purity ceramic insulator and aligned coaxially to tight tolerances.

buildSteps.title: Build the vacuum test stand
buildSteps.detail: A large chamber with high pumping speed, a high-current supply and a thrust stand is prepared for firing tests.

buildSteps.title: Fire in pulses and quasi-steady bursts
buildSteps.detail: Short runs measure thrust, exhaust velocity and efficiency while limiting electrode heating.

buildSteps.title: Run endurance tests
buildSteps.detail: Longer firings track cathode erosion, insulator contamination and changes in performance.

buildSteps.title: Qualify for space
buildSteps.detail: Vibration, thermal-vacuum and electromagnetic-compatibility testing proves the unit survives launch and operates in vacuum.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with the spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: The thruster is matched to the power system, propellant tank and thermal radiators, then commissioned in orbit.

prerequisites.tech: High-power spacecraft power (100 kW to megawatts)
prerequisites.why: solar arrays and nuclear reactors at this scale have been studied but not routinely flown.
cathode wear limits lifetime; no high-power MPD has run for the thousands of hours a mission needs.
converters at hundreds of kilowatts with low mass are not yet standard space hardware.
at high power, radiators become a major fraction of the spacecraft.
argon, lithium and ammonia handling is understood from other electric thrusters.

pathway.milestone: laboratory firing at hundreds of kilowatts in pulsed or quasi-steady mode
pathway.unlocks: data on thrust scaling and electrode wear.

pathway.milestone: continuous multi-hundred-kilowatt operation with a qualified lifetime
pathway.unlocks: a credible power-processing and thermal design for flight.

pathway.milestone: in-orbit demonstration on an orbit-raising or cargo vehicle
pathway.unlocks: confidence in arc stability and electromagnetic cleanliness.
fast, high-payload transport between low Earth orbit and higher orbits or the Moon.
